title: Introduce HSM Session Lease Operator, cert-revocation sweep, and Helm preflight rollback hooks
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Adds an HSM session lease controller, automated certificate revocation sweep, and Helm preflight + rollback-safe hooks. Ops-only features; non-breaking. See upgrade notes for preflight requirements.

description:
Summary: Adds an HSM Session Lease Operator that manages ephemeral session leases to prevent long-lived pinned sessions from exhausting HSM slots, introduces an automated certificate revocation sweep that identifies certs hitting CRLs/OCSP errors and schedules rotations, and extends the Helm chart with preflight checks and rollback-safe job hooks. Motivation: Customers running Redwood Private on-prem hit HSM session saturation during heavy deploys and certificate revocation events caused unplanned failovers. This PR provides an ops-first automation layer to reduce manual intervention and to make upgrades/rollbacks safer.

Implementation details: The HSM Session Lease Operator is implemented as a controller with a small CRD (HsmSessionLease). It tracks active sessions, enforces a configurable max-lease-duration, and performs graceful eviction with a configurable grace window to allow in-flight requests to finish. The operator supports two lease backends: direct HSM bindings (pkcs11 connector) and Vault-transit-backed synthetic leases. Lease ownership is reconciled using leader election and a lightweight heartbeat.

Certificate Revocation Sweep: A periodic job scans configured cert stores (K8s Secrets and Vault PKI paths), checks CRL/OCSP endpoints in parallel with rate-limited clients, and marks certificates that meet the revocation/expiry policy for rotation. The sweep supports a dry-run mode and a staged rotation policy to avoid mass rekeying. Rotation actions produce SealedSecret-compatible artifacts for air-gapped environments.

Helm changes: A new preflight hook (hsm-preflight-job) runs as a pre-upgrade hook to validate HSM connectivity, token validity, and required capabilities. There is also a rollback-safeguard hook that runs the revocation-sweep in dry-run to ensure a rollback will not leave the cluster with revoked certs. Chart flags (hsm.sessionLease.enabled, certs.revocationSweep.enabled) default to disabled to avoid unexpected behavior on existing installs.

Terraform: Adds optional variables to enable lease IAM/KMS policies and a scheduled job resource for the sweep when operating in managed cloud environments. The module is backward compatible when flags are not set.

Upgrade and rollback guidance: This change is non-breaking but operationally significant. Operators should enable the preflight hook and run the preflight job manually in a staging environment. Upgrades should be staged: enable session lease controller in monitoring mode for 24 hours (no eviction) to observe metrics, then toggle to active. Rollbacks are guard-railed by the rollback-safeguard job which will block rollback if a critical number of certs would be left revoked without a rotation plan. Detailed steps are in docs/operation/*.md.

Security notes: The operator requires permissions to list/read Secrets and to create Jobs; when using Vault transit, it requires a lease-refresh capability only (no plaintext key export). All IAM policy changes are scoped and documented.

Tests: Unit tests cover revocation heuristics and lease reconciliation. E2E covers eviction and rebinding scenarios using a pkcs11 test HSM. CI: initial run failed due to gofmt and a brittle e2e flake; fixes pushed and pipeline passed on rerun.
